text:
morgan: FYI customer (luis) seeing intermittent GitHub OAuth failures — app returns "state mismatch" after callback. Happens behind an Azure AD reverse-proxy we've not seen before. Repro steps and logs pasted below.

luis-customer: Happens for some users only. If they refresh the flow works. Getting lots of `Invalid state` errors in our app logs.

morgan: Minimal server log for one failing request:
```
[2024-11-07T14:12:03Z] auth.callback start: request_id=rid-9a3f
GET /auth/callback?code=SplX...&state=st-abc123 HTTP/1.1
Host: app.customer.example
User-Agent: GitHub-HubFlow
Cookie: session=SID:UEYJ-1122; other=val
X-Forwarded-For: 52.174.23.11
X-Forwarded-Host: app.customer.example
X-Forwarded-Proto: http
X-Forwarded-Port: 80

handler looked up session for cookie SID:UEYJ-1122 -> session.state = st-x9z9 (does not match st-abc123)
Result: state_mismatch -> redirect /login?error=state_mismatch
```

devon: Can you confirm whether the proxy rewrites cookies or normalizes ports? That X-Forwarded-Proto/Port look suspicious (proxy terminating TLS but sending http/80). If the browser is using 443 and proxy sets a different host/port, cookie scoping might mismatch.

hana: Azure AD Application Gateway / Front Door sometimes does cookie affinity pooling. If backend pool has sticky session disabled or misconfigured, a subsequent callback can land on a different backend with a different session store (or stale cookie). We had a bug like this in prod before.

jacob: Also double-check PKCE flow: do we see code_verifier present in the session? If the session is swapped, the verifier will be missing and we'll reject. But the symptom looks like session cookie value points to a different session record.

morgan: Customer provided browser network capture showing two nearly simultaneous requests during the callback window — one to `/auth/start` then callback to `/auth/callback` but the backend replies came from different backends. They included a proxy trace id: `proxy-trace=pt-44ef` in headers.

infra-bot: noted config change: `azure-proxy-route-12` updated @ 2024-11-07T00:30:12Z (preserve_cookie_path=false, preserve_proto=false) — change rolled 3h before incidents spiked.

devon: OK that matches. Most likely the proxy rewrite removed `Secure`/`SameSite` or changed the cookie path causing the browser to send an unexpected cookie to the callback. Two fast actions: 1) ask proxy team to re-enable preserve_cookie_path + preserve_proto; 2) add extra debug logging in auth callback for `Set-Cookie` vs incoming `Cookie` and log session ID hash (PII-safe) so we can correlate.

morgan: Repro steps customer gave (simple loop):
```bash
# start auth flow, capture cookies, then hit callback repeatedly to reproduce race
for i in {1..50}; do 
  curl -v -b cookies.txt 'https://app.customer.example/auth/callback?code=...&state=st-abc123' 
done
```
They say ~1/8 runs produce state mismatch.

hana: I can add temporary logs: on mismatch, log `incoming_cookie_session=<hex> expected_session=<hex> trace_id=<header proxy-trace>` and return 403 with HTML that hints "session swapped" for internal debugging. Will push a small change to auth handler (no customer-visible PID).

morgan: Customer asked for a workaround to unblock users now. Suggestions?

devon: Two short-term workarounds: 1) ask them to enable TLS passthrough (so proxy doesn't rewrite proto/port) OR 2) instruct users to start the flow in a fresh private/incognito window (avoids stale cookies). Also they can append a unique query param to redirect_uri to avoid proxy-level caching: e.g. redirect_uri=https://app.customer.example/auth/callback?v=uniq

jacob: Medium-term: we should harden the auth handler to detect likely cookie/session swaps and treat mismatches as a transient error that triggers a clean-start (clear session cookie + redirect to /auth/start) instead of a hard `state_mismatch`. That will reduce user-facing errors when proxy swaps occur. Need eng approval.

morgan: Customer trialed incognito workaround and confirmed flows succeed. They're willing to try our recommended proxy fix but asked us to coordinate with their infra.

hana: I'll open a follow-up internal ticket and PR to add the extra debug, link it here. Assigning to devon for verification with the customer's `proxy-trace` header.

devon: I'll reach out to customer's infra contact to get full proxy configuration (app gateway rules). Also will request they revert `preserve_cookie_path` and `preserve_proto`.

morgan: Thanks all. Action items for the thread: 
- hana: push debug logging (temporary) -> PR#7890
- devon: contact customer infra + validate proxy change -> ticket S-1123
- jacob: propose auth-handler fallback behavior (spec) by EOD
- morgan: share incognito workaround to customer and schedule 1:1 with their infra. :white_check_mark:

luis-customer: Confirmed incognito worked for 6/6 tries. Happy to coordinate with our infra on the proxy flags. Will share config exports when requested. Thanks! :pray:

morgan: Marking this as escalated -> eng-sre. Will move to postmortem if we see recurrence after proxy fix.
